articles.title: ‘A child pretending to be an adult’: Vanity Fair publishes scathing Taylor Swift exposé from over 100 sources
articles.summary: Taylor Swift is the biggest pop star on the planet, and she has spent much of her career being celebrated as a generous friend, a champion for artists’ right...
articles.body:
Taylor Swift is the biggest pop star on the planet, and she has spent much of her career being celebrated as a generous friend, a champion for artists' rights, and an underdog who fought her way to the top. But a new magazine profile is telling a very different story.

The lengthy profile, published on Monday, is built on interviews with more than 100 sources. It describes Swift as controlling and "punitive," and it questions nearly every part of the image she has built for herself.

Few artists have shaped their own public narrative as carefully as Swift. For years, she has described herself as an outsider growing up, saying in interviews that her friends abandoned her as a kid. Her songs have turned her breakups, feuds, and business battles into chapters of a story with her as the protagonist, and often as the one who was wronged.

The biggest of those battles came in 2019, when music executive Scooter Braun acquired her former label, Big Machine, and with it the masters to her first six albums. Swift responded with a scathing post on Tumblr , accusing Braun of "incessant, manipulative bullying," and she went on to re-record those albums as "Taylor's Version." Her fans rallied behind her, and in 2025, she bought back the original recordings , which was widely celebrated as a win for artists' rights.

Swift has also been involved in plenty of public feuds over the years, including with Kim Kardashian and Kanye West, Katy Perry, and more recently Charli XCX. Charli's 2024 song "Sympathy is a knife" was widely believed to be about Swift, and Swift's "Actually Romantic" from The Life of a Showgirl was seen as a pointed response . Earlier this month, Swift appeared to put an end to feud rumors with former friend Karlie Kloss at a Kansas City Chiefs game.

Through it all, her popularity has only grown. Her Eras Tour became the highest-grossing tour of all time, she became a billionaire in 2023, and she married Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce in a high-profile wedding at Madison Square Garden this summer.

But the last few weeks have been rocky. Swift was reportedly urged to "take back control" after details from the wedding leaked, and she has found herself caught in a legal battle over The Life of a Showgirl . Even one self-described superfan recently declared that "the blind love era is over."

Now, Swift faces a rather scathing hit piece.

Vanity Fair's piece , written by May Jeong, never actually uses Swift's name, referring to her only as "The Star," and it gives nicknames to most of the other people involved as well. It is structured like a record, with "A side" sections telling the familiar version of Swift's story and "B side" sections offering a much less flattering one.

Many of the harshest claims come from anonymous sources. A music industry executive, referred to as "The Exec," described Swift bluntly.

The same executive compared Swift's social circle to the villain of Mean Girls , saying, "It's truly Regina George."

Another source, described as a person who used to be close with Swift, said that she "loves to smack people in the head" in a figurative sense, as a way of disciplining people. That source also said Swift has a pattern of cutting people out of her life.

"Nobody is beyond reproach with her. If you don't see it her way, she comes after you," the source said.

The piece also runs through many of Swift's feuds over the years, including her rift with Katy Perry, who is referred to as "The California Girl." Jeong described Perry as "an adult pretending to be a child," and then turned the line around on Swift, writing that she "might be a child pretending to be an adult."

According to Jeong, many people refused to speak on the record, and one former collaborator even advised Jeong to turn down the assignment. Swift declined to comment for the story.

articles.title: Country singer Drake White admits he still fears another stroke seven years after nearly dying
articles.summary: Drake White reveals the fear of another stroke lingers seven years after his hemorrhagic stroke, and how faith and Navy SEALs help him cope.
articles.body: Seven years after suffering a hemorrhagic stroke that nearly killed him in 2019, country music star Drake White admits he still lives with the lingering fear of suffering another medical emergency. Speaking exclusively to Fox News Digital at the third-annual Benefit For The Brain event in Nashville, the 43-year-old singer opened up about the lasting physical and mental toll of his health battle — and how he has learned to channel that anxiety into purpose. "The fear of having another stroke is always there," White said. "Once your nervous system goes through that, it’s imprinted on it. You can work yourself into a tizzy, you can work yourself into anxiety attacks, and your heart rate gets up, your blood pressure gets going. So, it's about learning how to deal with that and breathe through it." COUNTRY SINGER DRAKE WHITE DESCRIBES ‘GUNSHOT’ MOMENT HIS BRAIN RUPTURED MID-CONCERT: ‘I KNEW I WAS DYING’ White credited both his background as an athlete and the support of friends — including several Navy SEALs in attendance at the benefit — with teaching him how to manage anxiety and high-stress situations. "Just being confident in people saying, 'Hey, you're helping, keep going,'" he explained. "Because there are so many days that I don't want to keep going. So yeah, I fear sometimes, but there's a lot of good things in fear, too. You pay attention when you're scared." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE Even seven years later, the memory of his near-death experience remains vivid. "It feels just as real today," White said. "For me, I had a real-life experience where I witnessed a near-death experience. To come through that — that'll never leave me. I'm 43 now; I was 35 when that happened. So for me, it's very, very palpable. Very, very real." "The thing is, God meets you where you're at," he added. "I don't care who you are, what you believe or what you think, if you cry out to Jesus, you cry out to God ... God's gonna meet you where you're at, and He's gonna come to you. And that's what happened. It was as clear as that." In an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital earlier this year, White reflected further on that life-changing moment and how leaning on his faith carried him through recovery. CAN FAITH HELP PATIENTS HEAL? VETERAN DOCTOR REVEALS WHAT HE'S WITNESSED FIRSTHAND Before hitting the road with Zac Brown in 2019, White was diagnosed with a rare brain condition called arteriovenous malformation (AVM). Having already undergone four surgeries, White said doctors told him the chance of a rupture was less than 1%. He decided to take the risk and continue touring. His worst nightmare unfolded while doing what he loved most: performing. REALITY STAR DR PIMPLE POPPER SUFFERED A STROKE WHILE FILMING HER SHOW, SAYS PART OF HER BRAIN 'DIED' "We just took the stage in Roanoke, Virginia. It was probably 98 degrees and cotton candy skies, beautiful, 2,500 people out there. And I tore into three or four songs and I just felt a tick," White recalled. "I felt my left arm, my fingers tingling, kind of numbness. And then I heard what I call a gunshot. It literally sounded like an audible gunshot behind my left ear. And when it snapped, if you look at the video back, you can see me trying to push through it." PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE "I grew up in Alabama where you just kind of keep pushing, keep going, and I tried to do that, and I couldn't speak," he continued. "I couldn't think, and the cotton candy sky became the grass, and the grass became the sky. Everything flipped upside down ... Everything slowed way down, and it just felt like I was walking in quicksand, and everything was heavy. My left arm was heavy, my left foot was heavy, and I knew right then, I was like, 'Well, dang, I'm having a stroke.'" White immediately remembered his doctors' warnings about what would happen if the AVM ruptured. "They told me, 'If it ruptures, you would have a very good chance of death,'" he said. "Death was kind of it. And so I just remember thinking: Keep breathing, keep praying, and get me to the hospital." RUDY GIULIANI REVEALS HE HAD 'SPIRITUAL EXPERIENCE' WHILE IN PNEUMONIA-RELATED COMA White was rushed to a local hospital and administered a coagulant that stopped the brain bleed. "That ultimately saved my life, but in that process, [I] saw angels, had the whole near-death experience, talked to God, the whole thing," he said. "It humbled me down to my knees. I realized that rock bottom had a basement. It really got me to a spot where I didn't know if I was gonna survive." At the time, the country singer was left paralyzed on his left side and uncertain of his future. "That was when the mental battle started," White said. "The doctors came in and told me that I'd had a hemorrhagic stroke and that I had a long road ahead of me. They didn't say this directly, but I heard them murmuring that I'd be lucky to walk again, much less get back on stage." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "That's when my world kind of crashed in around me," he added. "I was thinking, 'I've put so much time into this, and I've been so passionate about it. What am I going to do now? I've got a bedpan and I can't even feed myself.'" Amid his recovery, White and his wife, Alex, were hit with another tragedy six years after his stroke. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER In September 2025, the couple — who are parents to a 3-year-old son — announced the death of their newborn daughter, Della Elizabeth. During this time, White leaned heavily on his family, friends and faith. Looking back, he describes his previous interaction with God during his near-death experience as "very peaceful." "My faith, I like to describe it like this: The sun feels different on my cheek than it does on your cheek," he said. "I am a Jesus-following guy that believes in that wholeheartedly. Met Him, saw Him, talked to Him. It's as real as me and you talking right now ... He was like, 'What's going on? Tell me what's up. ' It was the most peaceful I'd ever been in my life in that moment." "I was not scared," he continued. "It's just like a transition. I could feel it. It was palpable. You know what I mean? I could touch it ... Whatever faith is for you, it meets you where you are. It meets you where you are in a hospital bed or in a car wreck or whatever it is. It met me where I was." Now, White is turning his new perspective into action through his Benefit For The Brain concert. Following two consecutive sold-out shows, the event’s third installment once again united major musical talent and passionate advocates to raise awareness and funds for brain and mental health. For White, hosting the event is the fulfillment of a vow he made while fighting for his life. "For me, it was just a promise to myself and a promise to God that if He let me out of the hospital — if He would get me to a place where I could live again — that I would help give back to people and show people how I got from the darkness to the light," White said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "That promise was just something I could drive towards," he continued. "If you have a purpose, and you find that purpose and push towards it, then your life starts to make sense. None of that stuff made sense to me when I was going through it — there were a lot of whines and a lot of howls. But when you start seeing other people come up and say, 'Hey, you helped me through this,' or 'You helped me through cancer,' or 'You helped me through losing my son or daughter' — who am I to even be complaining about what I had to go through if I get an opportunity to help people? "

articles.title: 'It feels more like an entire lifetime than one year': Hema Malini remembers Dharmendra on his first death anniversary - Exclusive
articles.summary: Hema Malini pays heartfelt tribute to her late husband Dharmendra on his first death anniversary, expressing her enduring grief and cherished memories of their time together.
articles.body: It’s been a year since the entertainment industry lost one of its most beloved cine stars, Dharmendra. Affectionately known as the "He-Man" of Indian cinema, Dharmendra, 89, passed away at his Mumbai residence on November 24, 2025. Paying a tribute to him on his first death anniversary, his wife Hema Malini remembered his charismatic personality and expressed her grief, emphasising that time doesn’t heal every wound.Dharmendra’s death anniversary: Hema Malini misses him in every moment“It feels more like an entire lifetime than one year,” said Hema Malini on Dharmendra’s first death anniversary. While speaking to us exclusively, she added, “Do I miss him? Every moment, everything reminds me of him. It is said that time is the greatest healer, and that the pain becomes less. Wrong! The world moves on, whereas the grief for the one who loses a loved one remains frozen in time.”Hema Malini on her and Dharmendra’s bond: ‘He was my best friend’For Hema Malini, the loss goes well beyond that of a spouse. Dharmendra was also her closest friend, and she holds on to the moments they shared. “He was my best friend,” said Hema Malini, and continued, “I may not have been able to spend as much time with him as I wanted to. But whatever time we had together was precious and nourishing.”She mentioned Dharmendra was trying to prepare her for his inevitable departure. “But nothing prepares you for the loss.”Dharmendra and Hema Malini were one of Bollywood’s best-looking superstar couplesTogether, Dharmendra and Hema Malini were among Bollywood's best-looking and most admired superstar couples. Their chemistry and screen presence in movies like ‘Seeta Aur Geeta,’ ‘Sholay,’ and ‘Dream Girl’ were unmatched.Speaking of their pairing, Hema Malini is characteristically gracious, and her words about him are full of affection. "I don't know how beautiful I am. But he was definitely the most handsome man in the world," she said.Hema Malini also shared a beautiful, heartfelt post in memory of Dharmendra on her social media handle, expressing both her love and grief.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Billy Bob Thornton urges viewers to learn the real history behind Thanksgiving on Fox Nation's 'The Mayflower'
articles.summary: Stars gathered in New York City for the debut screening of Fox Nation's "Billy Bob Thornton Presents: The Mayflower," just in time for Thanksgiving.
articles.body: The stars were out on Monday night in New York City to celebrate Fox Nation’s "Billy Bob Thornton Presents: The Mayflower" as the iconic actor seeks to educate viewers, just in time for Thanksgiving. "The Mayflower," which is now streaming on Fox Nation, is a three-part historical docudrama that aims to strip away the myth of Plymouth Rock and inform viewers on everything from the deadly voyage across the Atlantic to Thanksgiving and one of America’s bloodiest wars. Fox News Media executives, Fox News Channel anchors, the show’s creators and other special guests gathered at The Whitby Hotel for an exclusive screening of the debut episode. "Thank God for Fox Nation, because they’re willing to tell stories of our history, which is awesome," Thornton told the crowd. BILLY BOB THORNTON SAYS HE’S A HOLIDAY ‘PURIST’ AS HE BRINGS BACK ‘TRADITIONAL’ THANKSGIVING AT HOME "The Mayflower" traces the Pilgrims’ death-defying Atlantic crossing, the fragile alliance forged between the English settlers and the Wampanoag people, and the devastating conflict that ultimately transformed Britain’s colonies into the earliest foundations of an American identity. "One of the things that I think we're quickly losing around here is our history. History is very important, and if you don't know where you came from, it's hard to live now," Thornton said. "I love history, I’ve always studied it. My dad was a history teacher, and I always want to learn more about stuff and I didn’t know this," he continued. "I knew the story they told us in elementary school." BILLY BOB THORNTON PUSHES BACK ON CELEBRITY ACTIVISM: ‘I DON'T KNOW ANYTHING ABOUT POLITICS’ The Academy Award-winning writer, actor and director said most people simply think, "’Oh, that’s great, the native tribe came over, and they had turkey'" — but the truth is far more complex. "The people who came over here on [the Mayflower]… a lot of people got sick, a lot of people died," Thornton said. He called for viewers to keep the trials and tribulations of the Pilgrims in mind when celebrating Thanksgiving with loved ones this week. "When you say your blessings to the people, maybe remember the people that suffered to get us where we are," he said. Fox News Media CEO Suzanne Scott, Fox News Media President and Executive Editor Jay Wallace, Fox News Media Chief Digital and Marketing Officer Jason Klarman, Fox News' Bill Hemmer, Dana Perino, Lawrence Jones, Martha MacCallum, Emily Compagno, Eric Shawn, Lisa Boothe, Paul Mauro and "House of Cards" actor Michael Kelly were among the guests for Monday’s screening and cocktail reception. FOX NATION TEAMS UP WITH JACK CARR TO TAKE VIEWERS INSIDE THE GLOBAL MANHUNT FOR CARLOS THE JACKAL While developing "The Mayflower," the team consulted a range of historical resources and experts, including historians at Plimoth Patuxet Museums, where portions of the series were filmed, as well as acclaimed historian Nathaniel Philbrick. The series is produced by AIRtime Projects and Terminal B TV with Thornton as an executive producer, alongside Geyer Kosinski, Tom Forman, David Metzler, Jordan Rosenblum and showrunner and executive producer John Ealer. "My only wish and prayer from you all is that you watch this as people who want to learn something and watch something wonderful that these wonderful producers and director put together with Fox Nation," Thornton said. Thornton currently stars in the hit Paramount+ series, "Landman," for which he received Critics' Choice Award and Golden Globe Award nominations for Best Actor in a Television Drama. His recent projects have also included the Amazon series "Goliath" and the critically acclaimed FX series "Fargo." Thornton has also starred in such movies as "Bad Santa," "The Alamo," "Bandits," "The Man Who Wasn’t There," "Friday Night Lights," "Sling Blade," "A Simple Plan," "Armageddon" and "Monster’s Ball," among other critical and commercial hits.CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP CLICK HERE TO SUBSCRIBE TO FOX NATION Fox Nation programs are viewable on demand and from your mobile device app but only for FOX Nation subscribers. Go to Fox Nation to start a free trial and watch the extensive library of your favorite FOX Nation personalities. Fox News Digital’s Laura Carrione contributed to this report.

articles.title: ‘Naughty’ vs ‘Nasty’: Universal and Warner Bros. Battle Over Titles for New Jennifer Aniston, Jenna Ortega Movies (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Two similarly titled movies are causing a war of words between Universal and Warner Bros. Pictures. The legacy studios are locked in a stalemate over dueling...
articles.body:
Two similarly titled movies are causing a war of words between Universal and Warner Bros. Pictures. The legacy studios are locked in a stalemate over dueling projects that sound alike and are set to hit theaters around the same time, five sources tell Variety .

The first is "Naughty," Olivia Wilde's raucous Christmas comedy starring Jennifer Aniston. The other is "Nasty," Mary Bronstein's psychological drama led by Jenna Ortega, which will roll out under Warner's new indie label Clockwork. Universal slated "Naughty" for Nov. 5, 2027, after registering the name with the Motion Picture Association in 2023, according to two sources. Clockwork, the nascent shingle run by Neon veteran Christian Parkes, has not officially set a date for "Nasty," though four sources say the film is also eyeing a November 2027 release.

Generally, studios go to great lengths to avoid delivering movies with similar-sounding names — much less launching them in the same corridor. "Naughty" and "Nasty" aren't alike in genre or subject matter. "Naughty," featuring Aniston and Peter Dinklage, follows a single mom who has to convince Santa Claus to testify at her divorce hearing. "Nasty," Bronstein's follow-up to "If I Had Legs I'd Kick You," revolves around an elite gymnast competing for a spot on the Olympic team while dealing with her manipulative coach.

Yet insiders at Universal and Warner Bros. feel the fact that the titles are basically synonyms could confuse moviegoers. Further complicating the matter is that LuckyChap, Margot Robbie's prolific film and TV production shop, is backing both projects. Universal and Clockwork declined to comment.

The spat is headed toward a formal review by the MPA, which has a 101-year-old department called the Title Registration Bureau to manage such conflicts. Arbitration involves a panel of studio intellectual property lawyers at the ready to hash it out. Although titles are not copyrightable, the TRB is armed with a 50-page document outlining rules of play and precedent, per one source, and its rulings are legally binding. The MPA declined to comment on the matter.

"Movies want to distinguish themselves, and the first way they do that is the title," says Jeff Bock, an analyst with Exhibitor Relations. "If they sound similar, there could be confusion."

Universal believes it should have dibs since it was first to file with "Naughty." That would mean "Nasty" either changes its name or shifts its release date. Insiders note Clockwork filed two alternative titles for "Nasty" with its MPA documentation, but the filmmakers are against using the backups.

Meanwhile, sources close to "Nasty" feel that Universal is "punching down" at Clockwork because the indie drama doesn't have the same broad commercial appeal as the Aniston-led holiday comedy. (Though Clockwork is a specialty label, it is owned and operated by the vast Skydance Motion Picture Group). Wilde is content to let "Nasty" proceed as titled, according to a person familiar with her thinking. LuckyChap is working toward a solution that sets up both projects for success without entering MPA arbitration, two sources add.

Disputes like these rarely become public knowledge, insiders say. And most often, studios work it out without involving the Title Registration Bureau. The group's last two arbitrations were in 2018. That's when Disney and Lucasfilm settled on "Solo: A Star Wars Story" rather than "Solo" to distinguish the Han Solo origin story from the 2018 climbing documentary "Free Solo." And Universal agreed to change its raunchy comedy to "Blockers" from "The Pact," a name that was already used by a 2012 horror film.

Renaming movies can benefit both parties. Ask Paramount and Sony, which released "No Strings Attached" and "Friends With Benefits" a few months apart in 2011. Both romantic comedies — one starring Natalie Portman and Ashton Kutcher and the other with Mila Kunis and Justin Timberlake — had an identical premise involving two friends who agree to casual sex without dating. "No Strings Attached" was originally called "Friends With Benefits," but the studio acquiesced to the title change. Any plot similarities didn't dilute the films' respective box office, with each one grossing $149 million globally.

To that end, movies with similar themes or ideas are less of a problem for studios. Bock points to 1998's "Armageddon" and "Deep Impact," two disaster films about comets on a collision course with Earth. Both were theatrical winners, with "Armageddon" earning $553 million globally and "Deep Impact" generating $350 million globally.

"Consumers might be fooled by something like that, but it didn't affect the box office," he says. "They turned out to be different, even though the synopsis was the same."

articles.title: Thomas Markle, estranged father of Meghan Markle, indicted on child pornography charges
articles.summary: Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan Markle, has been indicted on child pornography charges involving 35mm film negatives of minors under 12.
articles.body: Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan Markle, was indicted on child pornography charges. Markle, 82, is charged with possessing child sexual abuse material (CSAM), specifically 35 mm film negatives of prepubescent minors and minors who had not yet reached the age of 12 years old. He remains jailed in Florida after he allegedly cut off his ankle monitor earlier this month. If convicted, Markle would face a statutory maximum sentence of 20 years in federal prison on each count. MEGHAN MARKLE COULD BE DRAGGED INTO FATHER'S CHILD SEX ABUSE CASE, EXPERT WARNS On Oct. 30 and Nov. 4, Markle knowingly possessed 35 mm negatives that contained CSAM that had been mailed, shipped, and transported using any means and facility of interstate and foreign commerce, according to an indictment released Tuesday. "During both instances, Markle knew the images were CSAM and at least one of the images involved a prepubescent minor and a minor who had not yet attained the age of 12 years old," according to a release provided by The United States Attorney's Office for the Central District of California. THOMAS MARKLE ALLEGEDLY CUT OFF ANKLE MONITOR AFTER CHILD SEXUAL ABUSE MATERIAL ARREST "Court documents in this case filed earlier this month allege that Markle knowingly possessed CSAM in the Philippines and at two rented storage facilities in Los Angeles. Pursuant to judicially authorized warrants, FBI special agents searched the two storage units registered to Markle. Markle has rented both storage units since 2008." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "Inside the units, agents seized approximately 78 items, including slides, film negatives, and books that contained suspected CSAM," officials added. "Two images depict an adult man – whom a witness identified as Markle – with a nude prepubescent girl. The third image depicts a nude prepubescent girl in a room that appears to be part of a motel chain in the Philippines. The affidavit also describes additional photographs that appear to show Markle with children in various stages of undress." The FBI is investigating the matter. Federal prosecutors charged Markle with one count of possessing child sexual abuse material in a criminal complaint filed Nov. 5 before he was arrested in Florida. According to the 14-page complaint obtained by Fox News Digital, FBI agents searched two storage units registered to Markle and seized approximately 78 items, including film negatives, slides and books containing suspected child sexual abuse material. Investigators say Markle had rented the units since 2008 and continued paying for them through October 2026. Agents identified approximately 18 suspected illegal images among film negatives recovered from one unit. A witness, who had known Markle since the 1970s, allegedly identified him as the adult man appearing with a prepubescent girl in at least two photographs. The complaint did not name the witness. The investigation began after Markle Sr.'s son, Thomas Markle Jr., reported finding storage boxes containing suspected child sexual abuse images at his father's local residence and turned the materials over to authorities. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS Markle previously denied the allegations against him in a statement to the Daily Mail. "I’m shocked, I’m hurt, and I’m very upset that my son is making these accusations against me," he was quoted as saying. "I could never do what I’m being accused of. It’s the worst thing anyone could accuse me of." Meghan condemned the alleged abuse in October and explained her decision to cut ties with her father. "I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed," she said in a statement shared with Fox News Digital at the time. "I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications' distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them," she wrote. "I trusted that the authorities were doing the same for other families." articles.title: Shah Rukh Khan ditches 'King' look ahead of promotional spree; fans speculate a podcast collaboration on the cards - PICS
articles.summary: Shah Rukh Khan has ditched his salt-and-pepper look as he begins promotions for his movie 'King'.
articles.body: Shah Rukh Khan has ditched his salt-and-pepper look as he begins promotions for his movie 'King'. With the film's release just a month away, the Bollywood superstar was spotted at a hotel in Mumbai city, in the late hours of Tuesday night.Dressed in a suit jacket, jeans and tee, the star was seen leading the building with his team and security staff. Also seen with him was popular podcaster Raj Shamani.Pictures of the two making their way out of the property soon surfaced online, prompting speculation about a possible collaboration. While the sighting has given way to online buzz, there is no confirmation yet that the two met or were at the hotel for a professional commitment. It is also unclear whether their appearances were connected or merely coincidental.Nevertheless, the late-night spotting has got fans wondering if Shah Rukh Khan could be gearing up for an interesting conversation about his life, films and more. The timing of the sighting has also caught attention, coming just a month ahead of Shah Rukh Khan's much-anticipated film 'King'.The spotting also comes amid buzz that the film's team has a list of songs lined up for their release.The film is slated to arrive in cinemas just a week after the blockbusters like 'Avengers: Doomsday' and 'Dune: Part Three' hit theatres. The crowded box office has raised concern over the effect that the competition will have on the final box office numbers.'King' marks SRK's first major film release after the back-to-back successes of his films 'Pathaan' and 'Jawan'. Directed by Siddharth Anand, the action entertainer is scheduled to arrive in theatres on December 24, 2026, during the Christmas weekend. The film also stars Suhana Khan, Deepika Padukone and Abhishek Bachchan, among others.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Critics Choice Awards 2027: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash's ‘Ramayana’ shortlisted in two categories alongside ‘The Odyssey’ and ‘Dune: Part Three’
articles.summary: Nitesh Tiwari's ‘Ramayana’ has not only made its mark at the international box office, but the film is already gaining recognition from award shows.
articles.body: Nitesh Tiwari's ‘Ramayana’ has not only made its mark at the international box office, but the film is already gaining recognition from award shows. According to the latest reports, the film has secured spots in two technical categories on the shortlist for the 32nd Annual Critics Choice Awards.The Critics Choice Association (CCA) announced the shortlists on Monday, with ‘Ramayana’, titled ‘Ramayana: Rise of a Legend’ in international markets, making the cut in the Best Visual Effects and Best Stunt Design categories. In the Best Visual Effects category, the Indian epic will compete with ‘Dune: Part Three’, ‘The Odyssey’, ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’, ‘Project Hail Mary’, ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ and ‘Wildwood’. Dan Glass has been credited for the film's visual effects.The film has also secured a place on the Best Stunt Design shortlist, alongside titles such as ‘Dune: Part Three’, ‘The Odyssey’, ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ and ‘Jackass: Best and Last’. The recognition marks a significant achievement for the Indian production, placing it among some of the year's most ambitious international cinematic projects.Christopher Nolan's ‘The Odyssey’ has emerged as one of the leading contenders, earning mentions in 11 of the 12 categories announced. Denis Villeneuve's ‘Dune: Part Three’ and the Spanish-language film ‘La Bola Negra’ have secured eight mentions each. Meanwhile, ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ and Laika's animated feature ‘Wildwood’ have made it to seven categories.While 'Ramayana' has been shortlisted, the film has not yet secured a nomination in the two categories. It is now among the 59 films across 144 places in 12 categories selected by a special nominating committee. The final nominations for the 32nd Annual Critics Choice Awards will be announced on December 4, 2026, with six films set to compete in each technical category. articles.title: 'O.M Operation Mole' box office collection day 5: Mammootty, Dhanush film crosses Rs 100 cr worldwide; AP-Telangana leads state-wise gross; Tamil Nadu follows closely
articles.summary: 'O.M Operation Mole' has entered the Rs 100 cr worldwide club within five days of its theatrical release.
articles.body: 'O.M Operation Mole' has entered the Rs 100 cr worldwide club within five days of its theatrical release. The Mammootty, Dhanush and Sai Pallavi-starrer collected Rs 5.40 cr in India on Tuesday, November 24. The film recorded 6,108 shows across the country, taking its domestic net collection to Rs 61.45 cr. Its worldwide gross has now moved past the latest milestone, supported by contributions from overseas markets.Tamil remained the strongest language version, earning Rs 3.40 cr from 3,372 shows. Telugu brought in Rs 1.60 cr through 1,612 shows, while Hindi added Rs 40 lakh from 1,124 shows. The domestic gross collection has reached Rs 71.25 cr.Worldwide box office collectionInternational markets contributed Rs 1 cr on Tuesday, taking the cumulative overseas gross to Rs 29.50 cr. With the domestic gross included, the worldwide collection has reached Rs 100.75 cr.According to Sacnilk, an estimated 4,87,538 tickets were sold across India on Tuesday. Total ticket sales throughout the theatrical run have reached 48,75,195. The latest domestic collection represents a 14.3% drop compared with the previous day's earnings of Rs 6.30 cr.Five-day box office performanceThe film began its theatrical run with Rs 18.10 cr in India net collections on Friday, November 20. Saturday saw earnings fall to Rs 15.75 cr, before a slight improvement took the Sunday total to Rs 15.90 cr. The film then experienced a significant weekday correction, collecting Rs 6.30 cr on Monday.Tuesday's business registered another decline, bringing the five-day India net total to Rs 61.45 cr. The domestic gross for the same period stands at Rs 71.25 cr. Across these five days, the film has recorded 31,893 shows in India.Tamil version leads language-wise collectionsTamil remains the biggest contributor to the film's domestic box office performance. The version has accumulated Rs 44.30 cr in net earnings, accounting for 72.1% of the India total. Telugu follows with Rs 14.90 cr and a 24.2% share.Hindi has contributed Rs 2.25 cr, representing the remaining 3.7%. On Tuesday, the Tamil version alone accounted for 63% of the day's domestic net earnings. Telugu secured the second position among the language versions.The overall division between India gross and overseas gross currently stands at 70.7% and 29.3%, respectively.The Tamil 2D version recorded 25.44% overall occupancy on Tuesday. Morning shows registered 18.08%, while afternoon screenings reached 28%. Evening occupancy stood at 24%, with night shows recording the highest session figure at 31.69%.In the state-wise gross report, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana emerged as the biggest contributors, earning Rs 1.85 cr. Tamil Nadu followed with Rs 1.75 cr, placing it just behind the leading region. Kerala generated Rs 1.50 cr, while Karnataka contributed Rs 65 lakh. The remaining Indian markets added Rs 50 lakh. Together, these territories accounted for the tracked domestic gross of Rs 6.25 cr.The film features Dhanush, Mammootty, Sai Pallavi, Sreeleela, Naseeruddin Shah, Renu Desai and Indrans.DISCLAIMER: The box office numbers and the data in this article are compiled from public and industry sources. All figures are approximate unless explicitly mentioned, offering a fair representation of the movie's box office performance. These totals may change as official studio data is updated or as additional international market reports are finalized. articles.title: 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' box office collection Day 20: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash film earns Rs 17.50 cr; India net nears Rs 973 cr; worldwide gross reaches Rs 1,735.15 cr
articles.summary: 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' witnessed a fresh rise in its box office earnings on Tuesday, November 24.
articles.body: 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' witnessed a fresh rise in its box office earnings on Tuesday, November 24. The Ranbir Kapoor and Yash starrer collected Rs 17.50 cr in India, registering a 37.8% jump over the previous day's business. The film's domestic performance continues to remain strong, with the overall India net collection approaching another major milestone.The film recorded 15,817 shows across the country on Tuesday. The Hindi version accounted for the largest share, earning Rs 14.25 cr from 13,547 shows. Malayalam contributed Rs 1.25 cr through 829 shows, while Kannada added Rs 90 lakh from 445 shows. Tamil brought in Rs 70 lakh across 571 shows, and Telugu collected Rs 40 lakh from 425 shows.'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' worldwide box office collectionThe film's overseas business continued to strengthen its overall box office position. International markets contributed Rs 5 cr on Tuesday, taking the cumulative overseas gross to Rs 573 cr. The India gross collection has reached Rs 1,162.15 cr, pushing the worldwide total to Rs 1,735.15 cr.According to Sacnilk, an estimated 11,03,758 tickets were sold across India on Tuesday. The cumulative ticket sales throughout the theatrical run have now reached 4,03,30,546.Week-wise box office performanceThe film opened its theatrical run with an impressive first week. Across the first eight days, it collected Rs 564.60 cr in India net earnings, while the gross total stood at Rs 675.05 cr.Business during the second week, covering Days 9 to 15, amounted to Rs 299.15 cr net and Rs 357.10 cr gross. This represented a 47% drop compared with the opening week's collections. The ongoing third week has added Rs 109.20 cr to the India net total over five days. Its corresponding gross earnings stand at Rs 130 cr. The film has recorded 4,28,377 shows across its domestic run so far.The Hindi version continues to dominate the film's domestic earnings, contributing Rs 739.25 cr to the overall India net collection. This represents 76% of the total. Kannada is the second-largest contributor, with Rs 77.05 cr and a 7.9% share.The Telugu version has accumulated Rs 57.30 cr, accounting for 5.9% of the domestic total. Malayalam has contributed Rs 51.20 cr, representing 5.3%, while Tamil stands at Rs 48.15 cr, with a 4.9% share. The overall split between India gross and overseas gross is 67% and 33%, respectively.Day 20 occupancy across language versionsThe Hindi 3D version recorded 35.73% overall occupancy. Morning shows registered 24.77%, while afternoon screenings reached 42.46%. Evening and night shows recorded 40.46% and 35.23%, respectively.Tamil 3D screenings registered 37.52% overall occupancy. The morning session recorded 29.60%, followed by 17.20% in the afternoon. Evening shows stood at 18.10%, while night screenings reached 31.30%.The Kannada 3D version registered 32.14% overall occupancy. Morning shows recorded 24.18%, with afternoon, evening and night sessions reporting 38%, 35.73% and 30.64%, respectively. Telugu 2D screenings recorded 14.37% overall occupancy. Its morning, afternoon, evening and night shows registered 8.80%, 15%, 13.90% and 13.20%, respectively.The film features Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, Sai Pallavi, Sunny Deol, Ravi Dubey, Lara Dutta, Arun Govil, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh and Vivek Oberoi.DISCLAIMER: The box office numbers and the data in this article are compiled from public and industry sources.
